extracted.intended_audience: patent classification staff, patent examiners, and patent searchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on interpreting and applying the International Patent Classification (IPC) to classify technical subject matter in patent documents, including scope, definitions, categories, and special rules (e.g., chemical formulae, Markush claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: structured format and role
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions are prepared following a structured format, the most important part of which is the definition statement giving a more detailed explanation of the scope of the classification place. In the definition statement, relevant words and phrases are used which may be alternative to those used in the title and which can be found in the patent documents classified in the classification place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions also contain other parts, such as explanation of limiting and informative references associated with the title, interpretation of special classifying rules affecting the classification place and definitions of terms used in the classification place. Definitions are provided only for a limited number of subclasses and groups and will be elaborated for more subclasses, main groups and subgroups where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-limiting references
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-limiting references indicating the location of subject matter that could be of interest for searching are progressively being introduced into the Definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They do not limit the scope of classification places with which they are associated and are intended only to facilitate the patent search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical formulae and graphic illustrations usage
rubrics_metrics.description: In chemical areas, chemical structural formulae that provide a visual representation of the content of the classification place are introduced when necessary for defining their scope or for interpreting the scope of subordinated entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional chemical formulae are introduced in the Definitions for illustration and to facilitate understanding; formulae are available through hyperlinks in relevant entries. Other explanatory graphic illustrations may also be introduced where useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Covered" / "Provided for"
rubrics_metrics.description: When subject matter is stated to be 'covered' by/in a classification place, it means the subject matter has characteristics enabling it to be classified in that place. The expression 'provided for' has the same meaning as 'covered'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples are given (e.g., group A41F 18/00; B60Q 11/00) to show equivalent usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressions indicating residual subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrases like 'not otherwise provided for' or 'not provided for in groups...' mean 'not provided for in any other group in the same subclass or in any other subclass' and designate residual subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups worded 'Other...' cover subject matter not provided for in other related groups. Many subclasses include residual main groups (usually located at end of subclasses). Use of such expressions does not expand subclass scope except as specified (see paragraph 69). Examples: main groups 99/00 are special residual places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination subject matter groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Main groups worded '... covered by more than one of main groups...' provide only for subject matter which consists of a combination of characteristics not covered as a whole by a single one of the specified groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some groups designated 'not covered by any single one of main groups ...' may provide for both combinations of characteristics and subject matter not covered by any group in the specified range (example C05B 21/00).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'i.e.'
rubrics_metrics.description: The expression 'i.e.' has the sense of 'equals' and the two phrases joined by 'i.e.' are to be considered equivalent, one of the phrases constituting a definition of the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given (A01D 41/00): 'Combines, i.e. harvesters or mowers combined with threshing devices.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning and use of 'e.g.'
rubrics_metrics.description: The expression 'e.g.' does not limit the sense of the phrase which precedes it, but simply explains it by giving one or more examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purposes: (a) provide a typical illustration; (b) draw attention to something definitely included; (c) indicate matter covered by a group but with no dependent subgroup. Multiple examples provided (A42C 5/00; B62B 7/00; G02B 6/122 etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical connectors: 'A and B', 'A or B', exclusive 'either A or B, but not Both'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'A and B' requires the presence of both A and B in the same example or embodiment; 'A or B' implies presence of A or B or both; 'either A or B, but not both' implies presence of A or B but not both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit interpretation used to read group and subgroup titles and to decide classification when multiple features are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressions 'in general', 'per se', 'specially adapted for'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'In general' is used when indicating things considered for their characteristics disregarding any specific application or that are not specially adapted for a particular use. 'Per se' concerns only an item itself as opposed to a combination. 'Specially adapted for' indicates things modified or particularly constructed for a given use or purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Content per se' (H04N 21/80); 'Furniture specially adapted for children' (A47D); 'Receptacles specially adapted for transporting live fish' (A01K 63/02). Definitions of these expressions are cross-referenced to paragraph 85.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Or the like' meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: The expression 'or the like' emphasises that the classification place is not limited to the specific subject matter but also covers similar subject matter with essentially the same characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Non-abrasive sharpening devices for scythes, sickles, or the like' (A01D 3/00).

rubrics_metrics.name: Glossary structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A two-part Glossary is included: first part includes classification terms and expressions relating to principles and rules; second part includes technical terms and expressions used in the Classification itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Glossary referenced at end of Guide for definition lookups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope interpretation within hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of any classification place must always be interpreted within the scope of all its hierarchically superior places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation of a subgroup or group is limited by the subclass, class, subsection, and section titles, references, definitions and notes applicable above it (paragraph 67).

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles are broadly indicative; subclass and group titles define scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of sections, subsections and classes are only broadly indicative of content and do not define with precision; subclass titles (with references, definitions, notes) are intended to define as precisely as possible the scope, while main group and subgroup titles (subject to references/notes) precisely define subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: subclass A47D, references excluding school benches; titles of main groups and subgroups should be read with their associated references and notes (paragraph 68).

rubrics_metrics.name: Places may cover more than explicitly stated scope (68bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain circumstances, a place can cover more than its explicitly stated scope: (a) details/components specially adapted for or used only with the explicitly stated subject matter and not provided elsewhere; (b) combinations of the explicitly stated subject matter with other subject matter; (c) subject matter of a category not covered by the place and not covered elsewhere but related to the explicitly stated subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and cross-references (paragraphs 92–98) illustrate when coverage extends beyond explicit wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: How subclass scope is defined (compound criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of a subclass is defined by the subclass title, any limiting references following the subclass or class title, any limiting references appearing in groups of a subclass, and any notes appearing under the subclass title or its class/subsection/section title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each element can significantly alter scope; examples include notes defining terms in sections or restricting fields to other subclasses (paragraph 69 a–d). The scope of a subclass should always be understood to include all subject matter specifically stated in titles of its main groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions provide detailed explanation of subclass scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A more detailed explanation of the scope of a subclass is provided by its definition, where available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions specify exact boundaries of subject matter added to subclass scope by its main group titles (paragraph 70).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of main groups: read within subclass
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of a main group is to be interpreted only within the scope of its subclass and is determined by its title as modified by any relevant references or notes associated with the main group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a 'bearings' group in a subclass limited to a particular apparatus must be read as covering only features of bearings peculiar to that apparatus. Definitions may give more detail (paragraph 71).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance headings are informative only
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance headings are intended to be only informative and, as a rule, do not define nor modify the scope of the groups covered by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat guidance headings as limiting or expanding group scope (71bis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup scope determined by indentation, title, references and notes
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of a subgroup is to be interpreted only within the scope of its subclass, main group and any subgroup under which it is indented; it is determined by its title as modified by any relevant references or notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subgroups cover only a particular part of the subject matter of the parent group; indentation levels indicate how to read subgroup headings (examples B64C 5/00 series). Essential characteristics in subgroup titles determine scope relative to the parent group (paragraphs 72–74).

rubrics_metrics.name: File scope of groups (difference between scope and file scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject matter that should actually be classified in a group (the file scope) differs from the complete scope of a parent group (including its subgroups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a group gets new subgroups, its scope remains unchanged but the file scope is reduced; file scope is the residual subject matter classified in the group itself but not in its subgroups (74bis). For groups with no subgroups, scope and file scope are identical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary purpose of Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary purpose of the Classification is to facilitate the retrieval of technical subject matter; one and the same technical subject should be classified in, and thus can be retrieved from, one and the same place within the Classification — the place most relevant to be searched for that subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification practice should aim at consistent placement to optimise search and retrieval (paragraph 75).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention information vs additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: Two types of information in patent documents: 'invention information' (technical information in the total disclosure that represents an addition to the state of the art) and 'additional information' (non-trivial technical information which does not in itself represent an addition to the state of the art but might be useful for the searcher).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invention information is determined in the context of the state of the art using guidance from the claims, with regard to description and drawings. The rules for selection of classification symbols are the same for both types of information (paragraphs 76–80).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of subject matter (process/product/apparatus/material)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical subject matter may represent processes, products, apparatus or materials (or the way these are used or applied); these terms should be interpreted in their widest sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided for processes (polymerisation, fermentation, testing...), products (chemical compounds, articles of manufacture), apparatus (installations, tools, machines) and materials (ingredients of mixtures). An apparatus can be regarded as a product, but terminology guides interpretation (paragraphs 81–82).

rubrics_metrics.name: Places to classify technical subjects as a whole
rubrics_metrics.description: The Classification is designed to ensure any technical subject with which an invention is essentially concerned can be classified, as far as possible, as a whole and not by separate classification of constituent parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, constituent parts that themselves represent additions to the state of the art should also be classified separately (paragraphs 83–84 and example guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Function-oriented, application-oriented and residual places
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification places are organised to provide for: (a) things 'in general' (function-oriented), (b) things 'specially adapted for' a particular use (application-oriented), (c) particular use or application of a thing, and (d) incorporation of a thing into a larger system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places of category (a) are 'function-oriented'; (b)–(d) are 'application-oriented'. Places may be relatively more or less function- or application-oriented; examples and cross-relations (F16K, F16N, F02F, etc.). 'Residual places' should be considered only if no other place provides for the subject matter; expressions like 'not otherwise provided for' designate residual places (paragraphs 85–87,87bis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision rules when unclear between function-oriented or application-oriented
rubrics_metrics.description: If a particular application is mentioned but not specifically disclosed or fully identified, classify in the function-oriented place if available; if essential characteristics relate both to intrinsic nature and particular use or adaptation, classify in both places; if the above guidance cannot be used, classify in both the function-oriented and relevant application-oriented places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use (a)-(c) hierarchy in paragraph 90 to resolve ambiguity and ensure adequate coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of larger systems and novel parts
rubrics_metrics.description: When classifying a larger system (combination) as a whole, attention should be given to parts or details whenever they are novel and unobvious; classification of both the system and these parts and details is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: classify both vehicle wheel suspension (system) and a novel leaf spring (part) in their respective places (paragraph 91).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical compounds: classification by chemical structure and field of use
rubrics_metrics.description: When the subject concerns a chemical compound per se it is classified in section C according to its chemical structure; when it also concerns a specific field of use it is also classified in the place provided for that field of use if such field of use constitutes an essential technical characteristic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the compound is known and only the application is inventive, classify as invention information in the place for the field of use while chemical structure may be classified as additional information (paragraph 93).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical mixtures or compositions: classification by composition or use
rubrics_metrics.description: When the subject concerns a chemical mixture or composition per se, classify according to its chemical composition if such a place exists; if not, classify according to its use or application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If use/application is an essential technical characteristic, classify in both composition and use places. If mixture is known and only its use is inventive, classify in place covering the field of use as invention information and composition as additional information (paragraph 94).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation or treatment of compounds: classify in process place
rubrics_metrics.description: When the subject concerns a process of preparation or treatment of a chemical compound, classify in the place for the process of preparation or treatment of the compound concerned; if such a place does not exist, classify in the place for the compound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the compound resulting from the preparation is novel, also classify the compound according to chemical structure. General processes for classes of compounds are classified in groups for the processes employed when such groups exist (paragraph 95).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus or processes: classify by apparatus if place exists, otherwise by process
rubrics_metrics.description: When the subject concerns an apparatus, classify in the place for the apparatus if such a place exists; when no place exists, classify in the place for the process performed by that apparatus. Conversely, processes for making or treating products are classified in the place for the process; if no such place exists, classify in the apparatus performing the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no place exists for manufacture of a product, classify manufacturing apparatus/process in place covering the product (paragraph 96).

rubrics_metrics.name: Articles of manufacture: classify in place for the article or by function/field
rubrics_metrics.description: When the subject concerns an article, classify in the place for the article. If no place exists for the article itself, classify in the appropriate function-oriented place or, if this is not possible, according to the field of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: glue-dispenser specially adapted for bookbinding classified in group for 'applying glue peculiar to bookbinding' when no specific place for glue-dispensers exists (paragraph 97).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multistep processes and industrial plants: classify as whole if possible
rubrics_metrics.description: When the subject concerns a multistep process or an industrial plant consisting of a combination of process steps or apparatus, classify as a whole in a place provided for such combination; if no such place exists, classify in the place for the product obtained by the process or plant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subject also concerns an element of the combination (an individual step or machine) that element is also separately classified (paragraph 98).

rubrics_metrics.name: Details and constructional parts: classify in details places or according to applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Details or parts only applicable to or specially adapted for one kind of subject matter are classified in the details places of that kind if such places exist; if not, classify in the place for the subject matter in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details applicable to more than one kind of subject matter are classified in general details places if they exist; otherwise classify according to all the kinds of subject matter to which they explicitly apply (paragraph 99). Examples: umbrella details groups in A45B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of general chemical formulae (Markush-type): three-step procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: General formulae representing large sets of related chemical compounds cause classification problems; apply a three-step classifying procedure when general Markush-type formulae are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1: Classify all 'fully identified' compounds that are novel and unobvious when they are specifically claimed, products of a claimed process, or derivatives; a compound is 'fully identified' if structure is given by exact name/formula or deducible from preparation with not more than one alternative reactant and is characterised by a physical property or worked example. Step 2: If no 'fully identified' compounds are disclosed, classify only compounds with exact chemical name or developed formula and limit classification to a single or very small number of groups. Step 3: When only the general Markush formula is disclosed, classify in the most specific group(s) that cover all or most potential embodiments and limit classification to a single or very small number of groups (paragraph 100).
